title: OpenAI / GitHub neutered the GitHub plugin.
author: Legitimate-Paint2165
selftext: Yesterday the GitHub plugin in chat mode could create PRs and edit files no problem. Today it was updated to only have the ability to replace entire file contents. It now refuses to do any work on non-work tabs.

comments.author: Legitimate-Paint2165
comments.body: I'm extremely disappointed but I'm just going to make my own plugin for it..

comments.author: tribes33
comments.body: Yeah because it's a workaround for breaking Terms of Service, people use it to edit github repos when on Codex, they were using Chats near unlimited usage to delegate tasks and soon they will ruin it for everyone and make Chat cost usage

replies.author: Legitimate-Paint2165
replies.body:
No. Based on OpenAI’s current terms, there is **no blanket prohibition on using ChatGPT plugins/connectors/MCP apps to edit GitHub repositories**.  
In fact, OpenAI explicitly supports this kind of workflow:  
The Service Terms say Apps can let ChatGPT **“take action” on third-party applications**, with the user responsible for those actions.   
The App Developer Terms explicitly cover **plugins, custom connectors, Actions, and MCP servers**, and say they may allow users to “retrieve information or take action” through ChatGPT.   
OpenAI’s MCP documentation specifically discusses **“write or modify actions”**, including permission/confirmation handling for them.   
Most decisively, OpenAI has documentation for a **GitHub Enterprise app template** that explicitly tells administrators to configure **read and write actions** and says to test write actions against a low-risk repository.   
So things like your Let’s Dive Bot doing:  
ChatGPT → MCP/plugin → GitHub App → edit file → commit → branch → PR → merge  
are not inherently against OpenAI’s terms.

Doesn't seem to be against TOS.
